N1_alternative_routes.attempt: Computed the count vector and normalized empirical frequency for the displayed finite binary word and tested whether that statistic itself supplies a uniquely derived predictive interpretation.
N1_alternative_routes.mechanism: Relabel the normalized empirical frequency as the next-record probability law.
N1_alternative_routes.outcome: The frequency is an exact statistic, but treating it as a predictive law is an added interpretation and does not exclude other laws compatible with the same word.

N1_alternative_routes.attempt: Evaluated the likelihood of the same word under three distinct normalized Bernoulli laws and compared their different next-zero probabilities.
N1_alternative_routes.evidence_locator: The same finite history has positive likelihood under infinitely many other Bernoulli laws
N1_alternative_routes.mechanism: Infer a unique iid Bernoulli generator from the likelihood of the realized word.
N1_alternative_routes.outcome: All three laws have positive likelihood and give different future predictions; maximum likelihood becomes meaningful only after the iid model class is supplied.

N1_alternative_routes.attempt: Compared histories 01 and 10, verified that their count vectors agree, and applied distinct last-symbol-conditioned next-zero probabilities.
N1_alternative_routes.evidence_locator: Counts have already forgotten the order information needed by such a law.
N1_alternative_routes.mechanism: Use an order-sensitive Markov carrier whose sufficient state includes the last record rather than only counts.
N1_alternative_routes.outcome: The predictions differ although the counts agree, so the count projection has discarded information required by this admitted law.
